verses.1: Thus said Jehovah: “I am coming from the city of Babylon to those who dwell in Lebo. A spirit of destruction will come upon them.”
verses.2: And I sent foreigners into Babylon. They plundered its land, just as they had done it on a bad day.
verses.3: May he walk along that path, and may he be elevated by his own strength. And may those who are against him not be able to do anything against him.
verses.4: And they fell as victims in the land, like wild animals and pests in its corners.
verses.5: For Israel and Judah have not obeyed their God, the Lord of hosts. Their land is filled with sins, because Israel has violated the laws of God.
verses.6: They were rescued from Babylon. One man’s soul was saved from destruction. It shouldn’t be destroyed in the flames of war, for it is a time of vengeance for God. He will reward those who are worthy.
verses.7: A golden crown in Babylon, held by Jehovah. It commands all the earth. Because of it, nations will praise Him.
verses.8: Suddenly, Babel fell down. Her hair was torn apart. They took her clothes to wear as a shroud for her burial. But I will still be saved.
verses.9: We will destroy Babylon, and it will not be able to resist us. Then each person will go back to his own land. We will reach the heavens through judgment, and then we will be carried away to Shekhim.
verses.10: May Jehovah bring forth our righteousnesses, so that they may be recorded in the books of heaven regarding the deeds of Jehovah, our God.
verses.11: Let the gates be closed; let the rulers be filled with power. May Jehovah send a spirit from heaven upon the kings of Media, just as He did upon Babylon. This is an act of vengeance by Jehovah. It is a retribution for their sins.
verses.12: To the people of Babylon, Shau-Nes took hold of the throne. They established guards and prepared for battle. For they also knew that Jehovah would do as He had spoken to the rulers of Babylon.
verses.13: You have dwelt on many waters; your wealth is great. But in the end, it will all be destroyed.
verses.14: May the Lord, in His glory, bless you with His power. For you have been filled with greatness, and people have turned to you for help.
verses.15: He creates the earth with His power; He prepares the sea with His wisdom and planning. He turns the heavens towards Him.
verses.16: To the sound of his voice, the waters rose from the heavens. They rose from the edges of the earth in clouds, towards the sky. A wind was sent forth from his treasures.
verses.17: Everyone is ashamed of the knowledge of falsehood. Every person is disgusted by those who are deceitful. For they are full of lies, and have no true spirit at all.
verses.18: The wicked will be destroyed when they are punished. They will be consumed.
verses.19: It is not Jacob’s share that these things belong to him. He is the one who created everything. His inheritance belongs to Jehovah, the Almighty God.
verses.20: You have brought me all kinds of troubles in battle. I will be destroyed by you, and nations will be destroyed by you as well.
verses.21: And I will be broken in you, along with your horse and its rider. I will be destroyed in you, along with your chariot and its rider.
verses.22: And I will be destroyed in you, both man and woman. I will be destroyed in you, both the old and the young. I will be destroyed in you, both the married and the unmarried.
verses.23: And I will be destroyed by you, both in body and soul. I will also be destroyed by you, along with all my possessions and treasures.
verses.24: And I have destroyed Babylon and all those who dwell in Kashdim. I have punished them for all their evil deeds they committed against you, O LORD.
verses.25: I am your God, the destroyer. May Jehovah, the destroyer, destroy all the land. I will raise my hand over you, and you will be thrown down from the rocks. I will throw you into the burning mountain.
verses.26: And they shall not take any stones from you for foundations, for the foundations of the house will be eternal, says Jehovah.
verses.27: Shu-Nes came to this land. They set up altars in various nations. Nations listened to him. Kings of Aram and Ashkenaz worshipped him. Tefsar, the rider on the horse, was also there.
verses.28: Nations sanctified her; they honored the kings of Madai, their treasures, and all their possessions. They also ruled over all the lands under their control.
verses.29: The earth trembled and shook, because the thoughts of the LORD had been fulfilled: the land of Babylon was given over to chaos, with no one living there anymore.
verses.30: The rulers of Babylon stopped fighting. They sat down in their places. Their power became like that of women. They lit fires from their homes, and their smoke filled the air.
verses.31: He ran to shout out his news. He told the king of Babylon that his city had been captured from him.
verses.32: And those who were captured were taken captive, and the trenches were burned with fire. The soldiers were terrified.
verses.33: For as Jehovah, the army of Israel’s God, said in Babylon: “At the time of planting, it still remains in a state of growth; but when the time comes for harvesting, it is ready.”
verses.34: The king of Babylon, Nabuchadrezzar, ate me. He made me look like a hollow body; my stomach was full of worms. He devoured me from within.
verses.35: Hamasi and Sheri will say in Babylon, “You who rule over Zion, my blood will flow to those who rule over the cities.” They will also say, “Jerusalem!”
verses.36: Therefore, thus said Jehovah: “I will avenge your injuries. I will take revenge for your grievances. I will destroy her sea, and I will destroy her land.”
verses.37: And Babylon would become a place of chaos and destruction, with no one who could rule or govern it.
verses.38: Together, like wild beasts, they were driven away, like young animals in the wilderness.
verses.39: In their midst, I will destroy them; I will make them serve as a punishment for their sins. They will be destroyed forever, and they will never rise again. May the Lord have mercy on them.
verses.40: They were like cattle that were slaughtered, like sheep with their horns cut off.
verses.41: How was Shechem captured and its song destroyed? How did Samah Babel’s people end up in those lands?
verses.42: The sea rose over Babylon in the stormy waves.
verses.43: Its cities were like ruins of land that had been destroyed. It was a land where no man could live, and no child could walk through it.
verses.44: And I appointed Bel in Babylon as a ruler. I took Bel out of his place, and no more nations could come to him. Even the people of Babylon were destroyed.
verses.45: Let my people get out of her place, and let no one keep someone else’s soul captive under the power of Jehovah.
verses.46: And it will be heard in your hearts, and you will fear the sound that is heard on earth. It comes in the season of hearing, and then again in the next season of hearing. It spreads throughout the land, and it controls everything on earth.
verses.47: So now, days are coming. I will deal with the people of Babylon and all their land. All their cities will be destroyed, and all their inhabitants will fall into destruction.
verses.48: And let us destroy Babylon, both in the heavens and on earth, and everything that is in it. For we know that the conquerors will surely come against it, says Jehovah.
verses.49: Even Babylon fell; the ruins of Israel also fell. Even Babylon’s people were destroyed.
verses.50: From the ruins, they went forth to stand there. They remembered God from afar. Jerusalem shall rise again in their hearts.
verses.51: We were filled with shame, for we heard of their disgrace. Our faces turned pale, because foreigners had come to the holy places of the House of God.
verses.52: Therefore, behold, days come when the LORD will act. I will deal with its cities and all its land. The heavens will be filled with darkness.
verses.53: For Babel will rise up from the heavens, and its noise will be heard everywhere. Then invaders will come to destroy it, says Jehovah.
verses.54: A cry of pain comes from Babylon, and a great noise rises from the land of Kashdim.
verses.55: For Jehovah has saved Babylon from destruction. A great noise was heard from it, and its people were destroyed like water that flows away. The sound of their destruction was heard everywhere.
verses.56: For a savior came to Babylon; its rulers were captured. Their chains were broken, for the Lord has saved them from their troubles.
verses.57: And I have appointed her queens and her rulers. Her kings and leaders will reign for ages, and they will never be destroyed. May the name of the King Jehovah’s army be blessed.
verses.58: As Jehovah said, “The armies of heaven will be shaken in Babylon. Its high walls will be destroyed by fire. Nations will be destroyed in the void, and people will be destroyed by fire.”
verses.59: The words that先知耶利米 commanded were given to Shallum, son of Neriyahu, son of Makhseya. He went forth from Jerusalem as the king of Judah. In his forty-fifth year as king, Shallum became the ruler of Judah.
verses.60: And Jeremiah wrote down all the evils that would come upon Babylon. He wrote down all these things in a book for Babylon to read.
verses.61: And Jeremiah said to Sheriyah, “When you entered Babylonia, you saw all these things. You reported them all.”
verses.62: And Jehovah said, “You have spoken about this place as a place where no man or animal shall dwell there. It will remain a place of eternal rest.”
verses.63: And it shall be that when you read this book, you shall cover it with a stone and throw it into the depths of the abyss.
verses.64: And you said, “ Babylon will be destroyed, and it will not be able to rise again from the evil that I bring upon it. The words of Jeremiah will come true.”
